stem: Who is known as the father of genetics?
explanation: Mendel worked on garden peas and discovered the basic laws of inheritance. Morgan worked on Drosophila and Watson co-discovered the DNA structure.

stem: The organism used by Mendel in his experiments was the
explanation: Mendel used Pisum sativum because it has clear contrasting traits, a short life cycle and can be self- or cross-pollinated.

stem: An allele that masks the effect of another allele in a heterozygote is
explanation: A dominant allele hides the recessive allele when the two occur together. Codominant alleles are both expressed, so neither is masked.

stem: A cross between two individuals differing in one pair of contrasting characters is a
explanation: A monohybrid cross follows one gene, such as tall × dwarf. A dihybrid cross follows two genes.

stem: A person with blood group O has the genotype
explanation: Group O is recessive and requires two i alleles. IAi gives group A and IBi gives group B.

stem: The scientist who proposed the double helix model of DNA with Watson was
explanation: Watson and Crick built the model in 1953 from X-ray data and Chargaff's rules. Franklin provided the X-ray photographs.

stem: The sex chromosomes of a human male are
explanation: Males have one X and one Y chromosome. Females have XX.

stem: The father of a child determines the sex of the child because
options: his sperms carry either X or Y
he always gives an X chromosome
only the mother's chromosomes decide sex
he always gives two Y chromosomes
explanation: Males make X-bearing and Y-bearing sperms in equal numbers, whereas all eggs carry X. The sperm that fertilises decides the sex.

stem: The term used for changes in the DNA sequence of a gene is
explanation: A mutation alters the nucleotide sequence. Transcription and translation are steps of protein synthesis.

stem: Down syndrome is caused by
explanation: Trisomy 21 gives a person 47 chromosomes. Turner syndrome is XO.

stem: Charles Darwin explained evolution by
explanation: Darwin proposed that variations exist, more offspring are born than survive, and the fittest survive and reproduce. Use and disuse is Lamarck's idea.

stem: The remains or traces of ancient organisms preserved in rocks are called
explanation: Fossils give evidence of past life and show how organisms have changed over time.

stem: Enzymes that cut DNA at specific sites are called
explanation: Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors in genetic engineering. DNA ligase joins fragments.

stem: The structure of a gene is made of
explanation: A gene is a segment of DNA, and it codes for a polypeptide or RNA.

stem: A trait that is controlled by genes on the X chromosome is described as
explanation: X-linked traits such as colour blindness and haemophilia show a different pattern of inheritance in males and females.

stem: Haemophilia is a disorder in which
options: the pancreas fails to make insulin
the colour of skin is lost
explanation: Lack of a clotting factor causes prolonged bleeding. It is an X-linked recessive disease.

stem: In a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt), the percentage of dwarf offspring expected is
explanation: The cross gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so one quarter are tt (dwarf). Three quarters are tall.

stem: The phenotypic ratio of the F₂ generation in a monohybrid cross with complete dominance is
explanation: Selfing Tt F₁ plants gives 3 tall to 1 dwarf. The genotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.

stem: The phenotypic ratio in the F₂ of a dihybrid cross is
explanation: Two genes assorting independently give four phenotypes in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, from the 16 combinations.

stem: In a cross AaBb × AaBb, the probability that an offspring is aabb is
explanation: Probability of aa is ¼ and of bb is ¼, so aabb = ¼ × ¼ = 1/16, from independent assortment.

stem: In a cross AaBb × AaBb, the fraction of offspring showing both dominant phenotypes is
explanation: The chance of A_ is ¾ and of B_ is ¾, so A_B_ = 9/16. The fraction 3/16 is for one dominant and one recessive trait.

stem: A test cross is made between an individual of dominant phenotype and
options: a heterozygous plant of any kind
explanation: Crossing with aa shows whether the unknown is AA (all dominant) or Aa (1 : 1 ratio).

stem: A test cross of a tall pea plant gives 52 tall and 48 dwarf offspring. The tall plant is
explanation: A ratio near 1 : 1 shows that the tall parent made two kinds of gametes, so it is heterozygous.

stem: When red-flowered and white-flowered snapdragons are crossed, all F₁ plants are pink. This is an example of
explanation: Neither allele completely masks the other, giving an intermediate phenotype. The F₂ ratio is 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white.

stem: The AB blood group is an example of
explanation: Both IA and IB alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote, so red cells carry both antigens.

stem: A man of blood group A (IAi) marries a woman of blood group B (IBi). The probability that their child has group O is
explanation: The cross IAi × IBi gives IAIB, IAi, IBi and ii in equal proportions, so ii (group O) is one in four.

stem: A man with group AB marries a woman with group O. Their children can have only the blood groups
explanation: IAIB × ii gives IAi and IBi, so each child is A or B. None can be AB or O.

stem: A colour-blind man (XcY) marries a woman with normal vision who is not a carrier (XCXC). Their sons will be
explanation: Sons receive Y from the father and an XC from the mother, so they are normal. Daughters are carriers.

stem: A carrier mother (XCXc) and a normal father (XCY) have a daughter. The chance that she is colour-blind is
explanation: The daughter receives XC from her father, so she cannot be colour-blind though she may be a carrier.

stem: According to Chargaff's rule, in a double-stranded DNA molecule
options: the amount of adenine equals that of guanine
the amount of thymine equals that of cytosine
the amount of adenine equals that of thymine
explanation: A pairs with T and G with C, so A = T and G = C, and total purines equal total pyrimidines.

stem: A DNA sample has 28 % adenine. The percentage of guanine is
explanation: A = T = 28 %, so A + T = 56 %. The remaining 44 % is split between G and C, which gives 22 % each.

stem: DNA replication is described as semi-conservative because
options: both strands of a daughter are new
each daughter has one old strand
half of the DNA is not copied
explanation: The Meselson–Stahl experiment showed that every daughter helix keeps one parental strand.

stem: The enzyme that joins nucleotides to build a new DNA strand is
explanation: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to the 3′ end of the growing chain. Helicase unwinds the helix.

stem: The template strand of DNA reads TAC GGA. The corresponding mRNA codons are
explanation: mRNA is complementary to the template: T→A, A→U, C→G, G→C. So TAC becomes AUG and GGA becomes CCU. RNA has U, not T.

stem: The process of making mRNA from a DNA template is
explanation: Transcription is done by RNA polymerase in the nucleus. Translation occurs on ribosomes.

stem: The codon AUG codes for
explanation: AUG begins translation and codes for methionine. UAA, UAG and UGA are the stop codons.

stem: The genetic code is said to be degenerate because
options: most amino acids have several codons
every codon codes for several amino acids
some codons code for no amino acid
the code differs in each species
explanation: There are 64 codons but only 20 amino acids, so several codons code for the same amino acid.

stem: Sickle cell anaemia results from
options: an extra chromosome in the cell
a missing X chromosome in females
one base change in a haemoglobin gene
an infection by a blood parasite
explanation: Substitution of one base changes glutamic acid to valine in the β chain, so haemoglobin forms fibres in low oxygen.

stem: A person with Turner syndrome has the chromosome constitution
explanation: Turner syndrome is XO monosomy in females, giving 45 chromosomes. Klinefelter syndrome is XXY.

stem: The technique used to make many copies of a segment of DNA in a test tube is
explanation: PCR uses repeated heating and cooling cycles with Taq polymerase to amplify DNA exponentially.

stem: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to their
explanation: Negatively charged DNA moves toward the positive electrode and smaller fragments travel further through the gel.

stem: A plasmid is used in genetic engineering as a
options: vector for a gene in bacteria
explanation: A plasmid is a small circular DNA that can carry a foreign gene into a host cell and be copied.

stem: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell, produced in 1996, was a sheep named
explanation: Dolly was produced by nuclear transfer from an adult udder cell into an enucleated egg.

stem: Homologous organs, such as the forelimb of a bat and the human arm, show
explanation: They share the same basic bone plan, which suggests descent from a common ancestor, in spite of the different uses.

stem: Lamarck proposed that
options: characters acquired during life are inherited
all organisms arise from spontaneous generation
explanation: Lamarckism, 'inheritance of acquired characters', has been rejected, as changes in body cells do not alter the gametes.

stem: The peppered moth became mostly dark near industrial areas in England because
options: moths changed colour to match their surroundings
soot caused mutations in the moths
dark moths were less visible to predators
light moths migrated away in a body
explanation: This is an example of natural selection: predators ate more of the conspicuous light moths so dark moths survived and reproduced.

stem: Bacteria become resistant to an antibiotic mostly because
options: the drug causes bacteria to want resistance
the bacteria learn to avoid the drug
the antibiotic changes bacterial DNA to resist it
explanation: Selection by the antibiotic favours rare resistant mutants, which multiply, so misuse of antibiotics spreads resistance.

stem: Two heterozygous parents with the genotype AaBb produce 160 offspring. The expected number with the genotype aabb is
explanation: The probability of aabb is 1/16, so 160 × 1/16 = 10. The value 30 would apply to a class with probability 3/16.

stem: A cross AaBb × aabb is carried out. The expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is
explanation: AaBb makes four gamete types in equal numbers, and aabb makes only ab, so the four phenotypes are equally likely.

stem: How many different types of gametes can be formed by a plant with the genotype AaBbCc?
explanation: Each heterozygous locus doubles the number of gamete types, so 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

stem: A pea plant Tt is self-pollinated and gives 800 seeds. The expected number of dwarf plants is
explanation: Dwarf plants are tt, one quarter of the offspring, so 800 ÷ 4 = 200. The 600 is for tall plants.

stem: A woman of group A whose mother was group O marries a man of group B whose father was group O. The probability that their first child is group O is
explanation: The woman must be IAi because she received i from her mother, and the man is IBi. The cross gives ii in 1/4 of children.

stem: A colour-blind woman (XcXc) marries a man with normal vision (XCY). Their children will be
options: all sons normal, all daughters colour-blind
half of the sons and daughters colour-blind
all sons affected, all daughters carriers
all sons and daughters normal in vision
explanation: Sons get Y and an Xc, so they are colour-blind. Daughters get XC and an Xc, so they are carriers with normal vision.

stem: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 4 % of people have a recessive condition (q² = 0.04). The percentage of carriers is
explanation: q = √0.04 = 0.2, p = 0.8, and carriers = 2pq = 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.32. The value 64 % is p², the homozygous dominant class, and 20 % is q itself.

stem: In a Hardy–Weinberg population, the frequency of allele a is 0.3. The expected frequency of the genotype Aa is
explanation: p = 0.7 and q = 0.3, so 2pq = 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42. The values 0.09 and 0.49 are q² and p².

stem: Which of the following would NOT disturb the Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
options: Random mating in a very large population
Migration of individuals into the population
Mutation of one allele to another
explanation: The equilibrium assumes random mating, a large population, no migration, no mutation and no selection. Gene flow, selection and mutation each change allele frequencies.

stem: Meiosis helps to maintain the chromosome number in sexually reproducing organisms because it
options: makes cells identical to the parent
happens in all the body cells
explanation: Gametes are haploid, and fertilisation restores the diploid number.

stem: Which statement describes crossing over?
options: Separation of sister chromatids in anaphase II
Duplication of DNA in the S phase
Joining of two gametes at fertilisation
Exchange of segments in prophase I
explanation: Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, producing new combinations of alleles.

stem: During translation, the anticodon is found on
explanation: A tRNA's anticodon pairs with the codon on mRNA, delivering the matching amino acid at the ribosome.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a genetically modified (GM) crop developed for improved nutrition?
options: Golden rice rich in provitamin A
explanation: Golden rice contains genes that make β-carotene in the grain. The others involve breeding or farm practices, not gene transfer.

stem: The genetic make-up of an organism is its
explanation: Genotype is the set of alleles, whereas phenotype is the visible expression.

stem: Which of the following bases is found only in RNA?
explanation: RNA contains A, U, G and C. Thymine is replaced by uracil.

stem: A clone is a group of organisms that are
explanation: Clones arise from asexual reproduction or artificial cloning and have the same DNA.

stem: Insulin for diabetic patients is now produced on a large scale using
explanation: The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria such as E. coli, which then make human insulin. It is safer than animal insulin.

stem: A Bt cotton plant is resistant to bollworm because it
options: has a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
explanation: The Bt gene produces a protein toxic to certain insect larvae. It is an example of a genetically modified crop.

stem: A carrier woman (XCXc) marries a man with normal vision (XCY). The probability that a son is colour-blind is
explanation: The sons get Y from the father and either XC or Xc from the mother with equal chance. The chance that a son is affected is ½.

stem: Why are X-linked recessive disorders more common in males?
options: Males have only one X chromosome
The Y chromosome carries the allele
explanation: A single recessive allele on the X is expressed in a male as there is no second allele to mask it.

stem: A part of an mRNA of 90 nucleotides excluding the stop codon will code for how many amino acids?
explanation: Each codon has three nucleotides and codes for one amino acid, so 90 ÷ 3 = 30.

stem: The wings of a bird and an insect are called analogous organs because
options: they have the same origin and structure
they are both vestigial in animals
they are made from the same bones
they have the same function, different origin
explanation: Analogous organs result from convergent evolution and do not indicate close relationship.

stem: The theory of the origin of life stating that simple organic molecules were formed from gases on the early Earth was supported by the experiment of
explanation: Miller and Urey passed electric sparks through methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour and obtained amino acids. Pasteur disproved spontaneous generation.
